## Common Pitfalls

- Don't truncate inputs when passing files or content to the API. If the content is too long to fit in the context window, notify the user and discuss options (chunking, summarization, etc.) rather than silently truncating.
- **Prefill removed (Fable 5 / 5.1 / 5.2, Opus 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, and the 4.6/4.7/4.8 family):** Assistant message prefills (last-assistant-turn prefills) return a 400 error on Fable 5 / 5.1 / 5.2, Opus 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Haiku 5.5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, and Sonnet 4.6. Use structured outputs (`output_config.format`) or system prompt instructions to control response format instead. (One exception: the fallback-credit prefill claim - when redeeming a credit with `fallback_has_prefill_claim: true`, the server accepts the echoed assistant message; see the migration guide's refusal section.)
- **Confirm migration scope before editing:** When a user asks to migrate code to a newer Claude model without naming a specific file, directory, or file list, **ask which scope to apply first** - the entire working directory, a specific subdirectory, or a specific set of files. Do not start editing until the user confirms. Imperative phrasings like "migrate my codebase", "move my project to X", "upgrade to Sonnet 4.6", or bare "migrate to Opus 4.8" are **still ambiguous** - they tell you what to do but not where, so ask. Proceed without asking only when the prompt names an exact file, a specific directory, or an explicit file list ("migrate `app.py`", "migrate everything under `services/`", "update `a.py` and `b.py`"). See `shared/model-migration.md` Step 0.
- **`max_tokens` defaults:** Don't lowball `max_tokens` - hitting the cap truncates output mid-thought and requires a retry. For non-streaming requests, default to `~16000` (keeps responses under SDK HTTP timeouts). For streaming requests, default to `~64000` (timeouts aren't a concern, so give the model room). Only go lower when you have a hard reason: classification (`~256`), cost caps, deliberately short outputs, or **`max_tokens: 0`** for cache pre-warming (see `shared/prompt-caching.md` -> Pre-warming).
- **Disabling thinking on Claude Opus 5 has two failure modes - prefer low/medium effort instead.** (On Claude Opus 5.5, `{type: "disabled"}` is a 400 at every effort level - use `low` effort. On Claude Sonnet 5.5 it is also a 400 - try `low` effort first, and if a route must stay thinking-off, send `{type: "between_tools"}` at `high` effort or below.) Watch for a disabled-thinking setting carried forward from Opus 4.8. With it, the model occasionally writes a tool call into its **visible text** instead of a `tool_use` block (the call never runs, no error is raised), and can leak `<thinking>` tags. Turning thinking on and lowering `effort` fixes both. If a route must stay thinking-off: **delete** any don't-think/don't-reason rule, don't name thinking tags, and add *"When you use a tool, you may say a brief sentence first. If no tool can express what the user asked for, say so instead of guessing. Do not include internal or system XML tags in your response."* Details: `shared/model-migration.md` -> Two failure modes when thinking is disabled.
- **128K output tokens:** Fable 5 / 5.1 / 5.2, Opus 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Sonnet 5, Sonnet 4.6, and Claude Haiku 5.5 support up to 128K `max_tokens`, but the SDKs require streaming for values that large to avoid HTTP timeouts. Use `.stream()` with `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()`.
- **Forced tool use removed (Fable 5.2 / 5.1, Mythos 5.2 / 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5):** `tool_choice: {type: "any"}` and `{type: "tool", name: ...}` return a 400 (`tool_choice: type "tool" and "any" are not supported for this model.`), on `count_tokens` and Batches too. Use `{type: "auto"}` plus an explicit instruction naming the tool, `strict: true` on the tool to keep schema-valid arguments, or structured outputs (`output_config.format`) when the forced call only existed to get JSON back. `{type: "none"}` is unaffected; `disable_parallel_tool_use` still works with `auto` (at most one call).
- **Tool call JSON parsing (Fable 5 / 5.1 / 5.2, Opus 5, Claude Opus 5.5, and the 4.6/4.7/4.8 family):** Fable 5 / 5.1 / 5.2, Opus 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, and Sonnet 4.6 may produce different JSON string escaping in tool call `input` fields (e.g., Unicode or forward-slash escaping). Always parse tool inputs with `json.loads()` / `JSON.parse()` - never do raw string matching on the serialized input.
- **Structured outputs (all models):** Use `output_config: {format: {...}}` instead of the deprecated `output_format` parameter on `messages.create()`. This is a general API change, not 4.6-specific.
- **Don't reimplement SDK functionality:** The SDK provides high-level helpers - use them instead of building from scratch. Specifically: use `stream.finalMessage()` instead of wrapping `.on()` events in `new Promise()`; use typed exception classes (`Anthropic.RateLimitError`, etc.) instead of string-matching error messages; use SDK types (`Anthropic.MessageParam`, `Anthropic.Tool`, `Anthropic.Message`, etc.) instead of redefining equivalent interfaces.
- **Error handling - catch a chain, not one broad class.** A single `except APIStatusError` / `catch (AnthropicServiceException)` / `rescue APIError` loses the distinction between retryable (429, >=500, network) and non-retryable (400/404) failures. Write a most-specific-first chain - e.g. `NotFoundError` -> `RateLimitError` -> `APIStatusError` -> `APIConnectionError` (or the Go equivalent: `errors.As` into `*anthropic.Error` then `switch apierr.StatusCode { case 404: ...; case 429: ...; default: ... }`). Per-language class names and namespaces are in `shared/error-codes.md`.
- **Don't research SDK types - write first.** If a type name isn't shown in the documentation included in this skill, write the code file from the namespace/package tables in the language-specific doc and let the compiler's error point you to the right name. Do not spend turns on fetching pages, SDK-repo clones, or compiling-and-running a separate reflection program to discover type names before writing - produce the source file first, then fix what the compiler reports. A quick `strings` / `jar tf` / `javap` against the installed SDK is acceptable for locating names (it returns in seconds), but don't escalate beyond that. A file with a wrong type name is recoverable; a session spent on discovery with no file written is not.
- **Bash and text editor tools are Anthropic-defined, schema-less.** Declare `{"type": "bash_20250124", "name": "bash"}` / `{"type": "text_editor_20250728", "name": "str_replace_based_edit_tool"}` - no `input_schema`. A custom tool with your own schema named `"bash"` is a different tool. Handler paths and security checks are in `shared/tool-use-concepts.md` § Client-Side Tools.
- **Advisor tool model pairing.** The advisor tool's `model` must be at least as capable as the request's top-level `model` - e.g. executor `claude-sonnet-5-5` -> advisor `claude-opus-5-5`. An invalid pair returns 400; a `claude-sonnet-5-5` executor accepts only the advisors its row in the pairing table lists (not Claude Opus 4.8 / 4.7 / 4.6, Claude Sonnet 5, or Sonnet 4.6). Pairing table (and which advisors return plaintext vs encrypted `advisor_redacted_result` advice) in `shared/tool-use-concepts.md` § Advisor. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **Agent Skills != Managed Agents.** To have Claude generate a `.pptx`/`.xlsx`/etc. via Agent Skills, call `client.beta.messages.create` with `container={"skills": [...]}`, the `code_execution_20260521` tool, and the `code-execution-2025-08-25` beta (Skills is out of beta - no `skills-2025-10-02` header needed). Do not use `client.beta.agents` / `sessions` / `environments` here - those are the Managed Agents surface, not Agent Skills.
- **MCP connector needs both halves.** `mcp_servers=[{type:"url", url, name}]` alone is rejected as a validation error - also add `tools=[{type:"mcp_toolset", mcp_server_name:<same name>}]` with beta `mcp-client-2025-11-20`. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **`inference_geo` is a direct top-level request parameter** - `client.messages.create(..., inference_geo="us")` / `.inferenceGeo("us")`. Do not put it in `extra_body` / `putAdditionalBodyProperty`. (Messages API only - on Managed Agents, `inference_geo` instead nests inside the agent's `model` object, never top-level; see `shared/managed-agents-core.md` § Pinning inference geography.) Supported on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and later; availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`. `response.usage.inference_geo` reports where inference ran.
- **Fine-grained tool streaming is not a beta feature; this skill's default is to turn it on for streaming + client tools (the API itself still defaults to buffered).** Set `eager_input_streaming: true` on the tool definition and call the regular `client.messages.stream(...)`. There is no beta header and no `client.beta.*` path. Do not also send the legacy `fine-grained-tool-streaming-2025-05-14` beta header. Python's `@beta_tool(eager_input_streaming=True)` and TypeScript's `betaZodTool({..., eager_input_streaming: true})` take it (before TS SDK 0.136.0, spread it onto the returned tool). With the field on, the API no longer coerces or validates the input, so the accumulated `partial_json` may be incomplete (`max_tokens`) or invalid - guard the parse (`shared/tool-use-concepts.md` -> Eager input streaming).
- **Cache diagnostics is beta.** Use `client.beta.messages.*` with beta `cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07`. Pass `diagnostics: {previous_message_id: null}` on the first turn and `diagnostics: {previous_message_id: <previous response id>}` on subsequent turns; the result is on `response.diagnostics`. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **Memory tool type is `memory_20250818`.** Declare `{"type": "memory_20250818", "name": "memory"}`. Go uses the beta-namespace type `{OfMemoryTool20250818: &anthropic.BetaMemoryTool20250818Param{}}` on `client.Beta.Messages.New`; Python/TypeScript/Ruby/PHP/C# use the non-beta `client.messages.create`; Java has both a non-beta `MemoryTool20250818` and a beta tool-runner path. Python/TypeScript provide `BetaAbstractMemoryTool` / `betaMemoryTool` helpers for implementing the backend.
- **Use a model the feature actually supports.** Some features are restricted to specific model tiers - fast mode is limited to certain models and platforms (§ Fast Mode), task budgets (Messages API only - Managed Agents session budgets have no model-tier restriction) are Claude Opus 5 / Claude Opus 5.5 / Fable 5 / 5.1 / 5.2 / Mythos 5 / 5.1 / 5.2 / Claude Sonnet 5.5 / Claude Haiku 5.5 / Opus 4.8 / 4.7 only (not Claude Sonnet 5), and the advisor tool requires a valid executor<->advisor pair. If the user's prompt names a model that the feature doesn't support, use a supported model instead and note the substitution in the output.
- **Don't define custom types for SDK data structures:** The SDK exports types for all API objects. Use `Anthropic.MessageParam` for messages, `Anthropic.Tool` for tool definitions, `Anthropic.ToolUseBlock` / `Anthropic.ToolResultBlockParam` for tool results, `Anthropic.Message` for responses. Defining your own `interface ChatMessage { role: string; content: unknown }` duplicates what the SDK already provides and loses type safety.
- **Report and document output:** For tasks that produce reports, documents, or visualizations, the code execution sandbox has `python-docx`, `python-pptx`, `matplotlib`, `pillow`, and `pypdf` pre-installed. Claude can generate formatted files (DOCX, PDF, charts) and return them via the Files API - consider this for "report" or "document" type requests instead of plain stdout text.
- **Server-tool errors don't raise.** Web search and web fetch errors return HTTP 200 with a `web_search_tool_result` / `web_fetch_tool_result` block whose `content` is a single error object (e.g. `{error_code: "max_uses_exceeded"}`) - not a raised exception. For web search, a success `content` is a *list*; an error `content` is an *object* - branch on that before indexing.
- **With `limited` networking, `allowed_hosts` also applies to Managed Agents web tools** (no hosts listed blocks both); `unrestricted` and self-hosted environments don't limit them. The organization's web settings in the Console also apply in sessions. **Finding:** the VM is CPU-bound during JusPrin C++ builds, and nothing else. Every window where the
VM sat at 100% CPU had 17 `cl.exe` compiler processes running (MSBuild `-m` on 16 vCPUs). Disk, memory
and network all had large headroom the whole time. Between builds the machine is idle and responsive.

VM: `jusprin-win-test`, project `elegoo-backend`, us-central1-a, n2-standard-16 (8 physical cores /
16 threads, Cascade Lake 2.8 GHz), 64 GB RAM, one 500 GB pd-balanced disk. Rebooted 2026-10-21 04:46 UTC.

## Evidence

Cloud Monitoring, per-minute, last 48 h (ending 2026-10-22 20:00 UTC):

| metric | result |
|---|---|
| CPU at >=90% of all 16 vCPUs | 271 of 2349 minutes, in 5 to 15 minute runs |
| disk read / write IOPS p95 | 139 / 193 (disk limit 3000) |
| disk read / write MB/s p95 | 4.2 / 17.4 (disk limit 140) |
| network rx / tx peak | 0.11 / 0.06 MB/s |
| host maintenance / host error events | none |

Guest 5-second sampler (`C:\PerfLogs\memstats.ps1`, CSV per day) over Oct 14, 21, 22:

- Every 10-minute bucket with mean CPU >=50% had `ClCount` of 17 or more. Buckets with CPU >=90% and
  zero compilers running: effectively none (0 to 2 samples per bucket out of ~100).
- Lowest available RAM seen: 21 GB. Pagefile peak 516 MB. No memory pressure.
- The sampler's own 5-second loop stretched to a median of 11 to 20 s, p90 23 to 33 s, max 125 s while
  CPU was >=90%. That is the "slow" feeling: everything interactive runs 2 to 5 times slower during a build.
- The Google guest agent's local health checks timed out at 03:50 and 16:14 UTC on Oct 22, both inside
  pinned windows (serial console).

Why it feels worse "the past couple days": more builds, not slower builds. Compile bursts started per day:
Oct 14: 25, Oct 21: 37, Oct 22: 32 (by 20:00 UTC). Minutes at >=90% CPU: Oct 14: 21, Oct 21: 64, Oct 22: 40.
Several Claude Code sessions are building in parallel worktrees (`C:\b\cal`, `prf`, `prfb`, `nouw`,

Secondary contributors (small next to the compiles):

**By Claude Code** — Reproduced and fix verified 2026-11-20 on the Windows test VM (jusprin-win-test, Windows Server 2022).

**Reproduced:** the released JusPrin 2.0.1 portable build (SHA-256 matches the release), with "report errors automatically" on and Sentry pointed at a local stand-in, crashed on 8 of 8 quits with exit code 0x40000015 (STATUS_FATAL_APP_EXIT); with reports off it exits with 0. So it hits every quit for everyone who turned error reports on, not a rare race.

**Fix:** stop Sentry from `GUI_App::OnExit` (new `JusPrin::app_closing()` → `stop_sentry()` → `sentry_close()`) instead of `std::atexit` inside OrcaSlicer.dll. Built from tag jusprin/v2.0.1 plus only this change: 8 of 8 quits exit with 0, and no crash dumps.

**Proof the close still sends:** with a local receiver as the Sentry server, the fixed build sent "session ok" at start and "session exited" at quit; the released build sent "session ok" and then a minidump at quit.

**Not proven:** why Windows refuses the upload thread during DLL unload; the fix avoids starting a thread there either way.

# Windows GUI test VM (GCP) — working harness

Drives a wxWidgets + OpenGL desktop app on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP,
headlessly: launch it, screenshot it, click it, verify the result.

Verified 2026-09-07 with OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 portable.

## The VM

    instance : jusprin-win-test
    project  : elegoo-backend
    zone     : us-central1-a
    machine  : n2-standard-8, Windows Server 2022, 100GB pd-balanced
    display  : virtual display device ENABLED (required, see below)
    login    : ssh as guitest with ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine

The external IP is ephemeral and CHANGES on every stop/start. Re-read it with:

    gcloud compute instances describe jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a \
      --project=elegoo-backend \
      --format="value(networkInterfaces[0].accessConfigs[0].natIP)"

then update winssh.sh / winscp.sh.

## Four things that had to be solved

1. **OpenGL.** The app hard-requires OpenGL 3.2 (src/slic3r/GUI/OpenGLManager.cpp)
   and exits below it. Stock Windows software rendering reports 1.1. Fix: drop
   Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (from pal1000/mesa-dist-win) next
   to the .exe. Reports OpenGL 4.2 on plain CPU.

   Mesa then auto-picks its **d3d12** backend, because the GCE virtual display
   exposes "Microsoft Basic Render Driver" as a D3D12 device — and that path
   crashed on the first frame. run-app.cmd forces the CPU rasterizer with
   `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`.

   Do NOT copy the whole Mesa .7z onto the VM: Windows Defender flags the archive
   as Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn and deletes it. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere and
   copy just those — Defender does not object to them, so no AV exclusion is
   needed. (The archive's sha256 matches GitHub's published release digest; the
   detection is a heuristic on the bundle, which also contains Vulkan layers,
   D3D12 compilers and media-foundation encoders we don't use.)

2. **A visible desktop.** A GUI app started from an SSH shell lands in a session
   with no desktop and screenshots come back black. autologon.ps1 creates a local
   admin `guitest` and sets Winlogon AutoAdminLogon so console session 1 is always
   live. Something in the GCE image clears those values after the boot that sets
   them, so startup.ps1 re-applies them on EVERY boot.

3. **Session isolation.** Display APIs, EnumWindows and Get-Process MainWindowTitle
   only see the CALLING session's window station. Run them over SSH and they
   silently report nothing — which reads as "the app has no window" when it does.
   Everything that touches the UI goes through `Invoke-InSession` in harness.ps1,
   which registers a scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive` so it runs in
   session 1, and writes its output to a file to be read back over SSH.

4. **Resolution.** Without a GCE virtual display device the guest falls back to
   Microsoft Basic Display Adapter with no EDID = 640x480, and the app's own
   window is 760x500. Fix (requires the instance to be STOPPED):

       gcloud compute instances stop   jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend
       gcloud compute instances update jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend --enable-display-device
       gcloud compute instances start  jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend

   Then 1920x1080 is available via set-res.ps1.

## Also required by this app

Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime is NOT present on a clean Windows Server image.
Without it the app puts up a modal "WebView2 Runtime" prompt and startup blocks
forever. Installed here as 152.0.4191.66 via the Evergreen bootstrapper:

    Invoke-WebRequest "https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?LinkId=2124703" -OutFile setup.exe
    .\setup.exe /silent /install

This matters more for JusPrin than for stock Orca, since JusPrin's UI is
WebView-based.

## Files

    startup.ps1      GCE windows-startup-script-ps1: OpenSSH, port 22 firewall,
                     authorized_keys, calls autologon.ps1. Runs every boot.
    autologon.ps1    Creates guitest + sets AutoAdminLogon. Idempotent.
    harness.ps1      Invoke-InSession / Take-Screenshot. Source this first.
    screenshot.ps1   Screen capture. Must run in-session.
    probe.ps1        Lists session 1's real windows to C:\guitest\windows.txt.
    focus-app.ps1    Closes leftover task consoles, maximizes the app window.
    click.ps1        Clicks the "x,y" in C:\guitest\click.txt.
    set-res.ps1      Sets 1920x1080. Must run in-session.
    install-app.ps1  Downloads the app, places the Mesa DLLs beside the .exe.
    run-app.cmd      Launches the app with llvmpipe forced, detached.
    winssh.sh        ssh wrapper. winscp.sh: scp wrapper.

## Typical cycle

    ./winscp.sh <local.ps1> guitest@<IP>:C:/guitest/
    ./winssh.sh '. C:\guitest\harness.ps1; Invoke-InSession -TaskName "X" ...'
    ./winssh.sh '. C:\guitest\harness.ps1; Take-Screenshot'
    ./winscp.sh guitest@<IP>:C:/guitest/shot.png ./shot.png

## Known gap

There is no current JusPrin Windows binary to test. The Build all workflow's
Windows job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with "could not find any
instance of Visual Studio"; last green Windows build was 2026-03-04 and its
artifacts have expired. Either fix that job, or install VS Build Tools on this VM
and build from the cached OrcaSlicer_dep_win64 artifact.

$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"
$log = "C:\guitest\exitcrash\build-progress.txt"
function Log($m) { Add-Content $log ("[{0:HH:mm:ss}] {1}" -f (Get-Date), $m) }

$env:Path = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","Machine")
$vswhere = "${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer\vswhere.exe"
$vsPath = & $vswhere -products * -requires Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64 -property installationPath -latest
$env:Path = "$(Join-Path $vsPath 'MSBuild\Current\Bin');C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin;C:\Users\guitest\.local\bin;C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64;$env:Path"
$env:CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM = "3.5"

$repo = "C:\src\JusPrin"

Set-Content $log "start $(Get-Date -Format o)"
git -C $repo config --global --add safe.directory '*' 2>&1 | Out-Null

# A real OLE drag-and-drop: starts a file drag in a small window of its own,

Add-Type @"
using System; using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
public static class Mouse {
  [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool SetCursorPos(int x, int y);
  [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern void mouse_event(uint f, uint dx, uint dy, uint d, UIntPtr e);
}
"@
$form = New-Object Windows.Forms.Form
$form.TopMost = $true; $form.StartPosition = 'Manual'
$form.Location = New-Object Drawing.Point(40, 300); $form.Size = New-Object Drawing.Size(220, 160)
$form.Text = "drag source"
$script:step = 0
$timer = New-Object Windows.Forms.Timer
$timer.Interval = 80
$timer.Add_Tick({
  $script:step++
  $n = 25
  if ($script:step -le $n) {
    $x = [int](150 + ($ToX - 150) * $script:step / $n); $y = [int](380 + ($ToY - 380) * $script:step / $n)
    [Mouse]::SetCursorPos($x, $y); [Mouse]::mouse_event(0x0001, 0, 0, 0, [UIntPtr]::Zero)
  } elseif ($script:step -eq $n + 6) {
    [Mouse]::mouse_event(0x0004, 0, 0, 0, [UIntPtr]::Zero)
  } elseif ($script:step -ge $n + 10) { $timer.Stop() }
})
$form.Add_Shown({
  $form.Activate()
  [Mouse]::SetCursorPos(150, 380); Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 300
  [Mouse]::mouse_event(0x0002, 0, 0, 0, [UIntPtr]::Zero)
  $data = New-Object Windows.Forms.DataObject
  $list = New-Object System.Collections.Specialized.StringCollection
  [void]$list.Add($File); $data.SetFileDropList($list)
  $timer.Start()
  $effect = $form.DoDragDrop($data, [Windows.Forms.DragDropEffects]::Copy)

  $form.Close()
})
[Windows.Forms.Application]::Run($form)
EOF

content.text:
I went through your five points. Two of my earlier claims were wrong: the crash-on-quit and HTTP 500 issues didn't come back, and my guess about the stuck chat was wrong. The file-drop bug is reproduced, and its fix already exists.

**Did the "resolved in next release" issues come back?** No. JUSPRIN-APP-2 (crash on quit), JUSPRIN-APP-1 (HTTP 500) and OBICO-SERVER-B2H are all still resolved, with no reopenings. B2H took 106 events from release 4127 and stayed quiet, as intended. The emails came from *new* issues. Sentry groups crashes by stack trace, and each Windows build (19045, 26100, 26300) produced a slightly different stack, so JUSPRIN-APP-9 got its own issue. JUSPRIN-APP-6 was the macOS copy of the Windows HTTP 500. My line "new copies keep coming" was misleading.

**Creality ffmpeg exit code 0 (MOONRAKER-OBICO-VP):** I searched again: every status, exit codes, the Creality OS tag, the MIPS architecture tag, this user, and the wrapper script's errors. The closest older issue is MOONRAKER-OBICO-VG, also "exit code 0", but it came from a Raspberry Pi on plugin 1.3.3, where ffmpeg really ran and stopped on bad webcam frames. That's a different cause, so I didn't merge them. It may be the one you remember. The local variables in VP's event show what happens on the Creality printer: the wrapper script prints `getconf: not found`, carries on anyway, and runs the printer's own ffmpeg, which exits 0. Why its stream ends is still unknown.

**Stuck chat (OBICO-SERVER-B2N):** verified, and my pause guess was wrong. Claude called web search *together with* three app tools. In that case the API waits and sends the search result at the start of the next reply. The failed request is only 454 bytes bigger than the last good one, but that reply alone was about 28 KB. So the app dropped the reply holding the search result. The reason: JusPrin saves a reply that ends in tool calls only after it sends those tools' results. If the turn ends first, for example the user presses Stop or sends a new message, the reply is lost, and every later message in that chat fails and is charged. I didn't learn which action ended the turn, because the app sent no event.

**Save failure (JUSPRIN-APP-8):** there are no local variables; native C++ events don't capture them. The stack shows where the error was reported, not where the write failed. On macOS this same path shows the real failing line, but on Windows it doesn't, because of how errors are re-thrown (in `ThrowStack.cpp`). That hides the failing line in every Windows report of this kind. What we know: the file opened, then the write failed twice in 12 seconds. A full disk is my guess.

**File drop on Windows (JUSPRIN-APP-7):** reproduced on the Windows VM, whose code page is 1252. The 2.0.1 `write_file` fails on `模型测试.stl` with Sentry's exact error message. The fix was already committed on `jusprin-dev` (e109da5c29, 2026-11-21) but never released, and that version writes the file. I couldn't drive a real drag-and-drop onto the running app on the VM, so I tested the function on the same path the drop handler builds. I resolved the issue in Sentry as "next release" and trashed its email. The same faulty pattern remains in `AgentHost.cpp` and `GcodeHistoryRecorder.cpp`; those break for Windows user names outside the code page.

**Security note:** B2N's Sentry event stores the user's JusPrin access token in plain text inside the gateway's local variables.

I posted a note on each of these issues in Sentry.

**Decision needed:** should I fix the stuck-chat bug in JusPrin now? It's yours to decide because it changes how the app saves AI replies, and that touches every chat. One option is to keep a reply as soon as it arrives when it carries a delayed search result. That's the correct fix, but it's a bigger change to the saving logic. The other option is to drop any search call that has no result when building the next request. That's small and also unsticks chats that are already broken, but it hides the underlying loss. I'd do both, starting with the second, which would unstick this user's chat as soon as it ships. Shall I go ahead?

content.text:
**Did I find the root cause of the stuck chat (OBICO-SERVER-B2N)?** Yes. I confirmed it from the server's own saved copy of that chat, though I haven't reproduced it in the app.

Here is what happened, step by step:

1. At 14:30 the user asked JusPrin to set up their Easy Threed K9 printer.
2. Claude replied in two parts. The first part started a web search. The second part brought back the search results and asked to read two printer settings.
3. The app read the two settings, but it never sent them back to Claude. The server's record shows exactly two requests for that message. A third request would have carried those settings.
4. The app saves Claude's reply only after it sends back the answers Claude asked for. Since it never did, it threw away that second part, and the search results went with it.
5. From then on, every new message sends a history with a web search that has no results. Anthropic rejects the whole request, and the user sees an error. This first happened at 14:33.

One part is still unknown: what ended the message early. It could have been the user pressing Stop, closing the app, or a settings read failing.

**Is the file-drop crash (JUSPRIN-APP-7) fixed in the next release?** I marked it "resolved in the next release" in Sentry, but that release doesn't exist yet. The fix is on the development branch, and no JusPrin version after 2.0.1 has shipped. So users on 2.0.1 still hit the bug. Sentry won't email again about crashes from 2.0.1. It will reopen the issue only if the crash shows up in a newer version.

**JUSPRIN-APP-8 (the "cannot write" error):** it's now ignored until 10 more users hit it. Right now 1 user has. I put its alert email in the trash.

**Do JusPrin issues identify users?** No. All five JusPrin app issues carry only a random id on each event, with no email, username or account number. The app never sends account details to Sentry. It sends reports only after the user agrees. My guess is that the id belongs to one installation of the app, but I haven't checked where it comes from. The stuck chat is different: it was logged by the server, which knows the account, number 264944.

**Decision needed: how should we fix chats that get stuck like this?** This is your call because one option changes the server and the other needs an app release. These are proposals; nothing is built yet.

- **Fix it on the server.** Before sending a chat to Anthropic, the server removes any web search that has no results. This works right away for every app version, and it unsticks chats that are already broken, including user 264944's. The cost is that it hides an app bug, and the server ends up editing chat history.
- **Fix it in the app.** The app saves each reply as soon as it arrives. When a message ends early, it marks Claude's requests as cancelled. This fixes the real bug, but only after the next release. Chats that are already stuck stay stuck unless the app also repairs them when they open.

My pick is both: the server fix first, so this user and others can keep chatting now, then the app fix in the next release. Should I build both, server first?

name: reference-sentry-resolve-in-release-semantics
description: "sentry.obico.io \"resolved in release X\" reopens on events from X itself; use resolve-in-next-release for unreleased fixes, and check the recorded anchor"
metadata:

On sentry.obico.io (self-hosted 23.1.1), an issue resolved with `statusDetails.inRelease = X` REOPENS (set_regression) on the next event whose release is X itself, and on any newer release; only events from older releases stay quiet. Verified 2026-11-02: OBICO-SERVER-B1J and B1C were resolved with `inRelease: "4052"` while 4052 was the live release, and both reopened within 5 hours from 4052 events.

An unreleased fix needs "resolved in next release" (`inNextRelease: true`): events from the release it is anchored to stay quiet, newer releases reopen it (MOONRAKER-OBICO-TT, anchored at moonraker-obico@2.2.3, took 21 events from 2.2.3 without reopening).

**Why:** the API rejects an `inRelease` that does not exist in Sentry yet ("Unable to find a release"), so "resolve in the version that will ship the fix" cannot be set for a future release.

**How to apply:**
- Never use `inRelease` = the currently deployed release for a fix that has not shipped.
- Use `inNextRelease: true`, then read the issue's activity (`set_resolved_in_release` data) and `statusDetails`: the recorded anchor must be the live release. For issues that were merged, or whose latest event is on an older release, the anchor came out stale (4031/4036 instead of 4052) and the issue will reopen on the next event from the live release. Fix those in the Sentry UI or verify after the next event.
- After resolving, check later that `set_regression` activity has not appeared.
- Related release-numbering facts: [[project-obico-release-architecture]].

content.text:
**Can I reproduce the stuck chat (OBICO-SERVER-B2N) reliably?** Not by hand in the app, but I can do it in two reliable parts. I haven't run either yet.

1. **The server part, on the local dev server.** I'd send the local server a chat whose history has a web search with no results, which is exactly what the stuck chat sent. Anthropic should refuse it and our server should return the same 500 error. This works every time. It needs a real Anthropic key on the local server and costs a few cents.
2. **The app part, as an automated test.** The app's chat code can be fed scripted replies instead of real ones from Claude. The script:
   - The first reply starts a web search and asks to read a setting.
   - The second reply brings the search results and asks to read two more settings.
   - The test stops the chat while those reads are pending.
   - It then sends a new message and checks that the request has lost the search results.

   This is also reliable, because nothing depends on Claude's choices or on timing.

Doing it by hand in the app with the local server isn't reliable for two reasons. Claude has to choose that exact sequence of replies on its own. And Stop has to land in the short moment while the settings reads run. We also still don't know whether the user pressed Stop. I'd run both parts before writing any fix.

**The file-drop crash (JUSPRIN-APP-7):** you're right, I framed it badly. It's resolved in the next release, and that's correct for a fix that's committed but not yet shipped. That's what the option is for. The fix will be in whichever JusPrin version ships next. If the crash shows up there, Sentry will reopen the issue, which would tell us the fix didn't work. Reports from 2.0.1 stay quiet, as they should, since 2.0.1 doesn't have the fix. I've added this correction to my memory notes.

**Identifying users in JusPrin crash reports.** This is a proposal; none of it is built.

- **Users who aren't signed in already have an install id.** The random id we see on every JusPrin event comes from the Sentry library. On first run it makes a random id, saves it in the file `installation_id` inside the app's `jusprin-sentry` data folder, and reuses it after that. It only changes if that folder is deleted or the Sentry address changes. No new code is needed for this part.
- **Signed-in users would get their account number.** The server's sign-in check (`/jusprin/api/me/`) already returns the account number to the app, but the app throws it away and keeps only the email. The proposal:
  - Save the number with the stored account.
  - Give it to Sentry at sign-in and at every start while signed in.
  - Remove it at sign-out, so reports go back to the install id.
- **Keep both linked.** Every report would also carry the install id as a tag, so a person's reports from before and after sign-in can be matched.
- **Still a guess:** that app crashes (not just reported errors) pick up the account number too. The library should pass it along, but I'd check with a test crash.

**Decision needed: should crash reports carry only the account number, or the email as well?** It's your call because it decides how much personal data goes into Sentry.

- **Account number only:** reports hold no personal details. You'd look up the person in the admin site when you need to.
- **Number and email:** you'd see who it is right in Sentry, but every report then holds the person's email.

My pick is the account number only. Do you want only the number, or the email too?
Account number only

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).
4	
5	## Upstream vs. fork attribution
6	
7	This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.
8	
9	- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
10	- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
11	- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.
12	
13	## Branches
14	
15	- `jusprin-dev` is the development branch. Start each change on a new branch from it and land the change there. It began at `975c703f08`, the merge of OrcaSlicer 2.5.0, and contains the earlier development branches `jusprin-newui` and `ui-walkthrough`; start nothing new on those.
16	- `main` is the stable branch and GitHub's default branch: the repository's front page, its issue forms, and the workflows GitHub runs on a schedule come from it.
17	  - Never force-push `main`, so that people who cloned the repository never have to force-pull. Only in an extreme case with no other way out, and with Kenneth's yes, may an admin lift the GitHub protection that blocks force pushes and deletion.
18	  - For now `main` is also the release branch: it moves forward from `jusprin-dev` when a version is released, and releases are built from it. This may change if a separate release branch is added later.
19	- `jusprin-v1` holds JusPrin 1, for fixes to that version only.
20	- `jusprin-v2-poc` holds the experiments described below.
21	- Take each OrcaSlicer release into `jusprin-dev` as `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` rule 10 describes.
22	
23	## Releasing
24	
25	`.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml` builds a release into a draft on GitHub; its top comment says how to start it. It refuses the commit until it has all of these:
26	
27	- The version, in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`, above every released JusPrin version.
28	- The release notes, in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md`.
29	- The Sentry secrets: `JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN`, the project the app sends error reports and crashes to, and `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG` and `SENTRY_PROJECT`, which upload each build's debug files and the pages' source maps. A platform's build fails unless Sentry then holds debug information with file and line for the app's own code (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh`) and a source map for each page as built (`sentry_page_maps.sh` beside it); the nightly build checks the same.
30	- The guide, `docs/guide/`, checked for that version. Run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai` on a built copy of the commit, fix every page it reports, and commit the pages with their pictures, skills and `docs/guide/checked-version.txt`, as `docs/guide/README.md` describes under "Before a release". That file names the version the check last passed for, not the commit. Ticking "Release without the guide check" on the workflow's Run workflow form skips this, and the draft's title then says so. A release started by pushing a `jusprin-release/` branch has no form, so it always needs the file.
31	
32	## Error handling
33	
34	Less is more. An error is **expected** only when the person can do something about it, such as sign in again, get more credits, update a key or check the network, and Kenneth decided what the product tells them. Every other error is **unexpected**: the person sees one generic sentence and a way to report the problem, and the report carries everything known, so that we can find the cause.
35	
36	Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is something that user can do nothing about, just show the user a generic error message and give user a way to report a problem. On the back end though, we need to make sure we send as much info as possible to the Sentry server so that we can do root cause analysis. And that's it, nothing else." And: "When it comes to error handling, less is more."
37	
38	The reporting function is `report_unexpected_error` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.hpp`). This repository has no expected-errors table yet.
39	
40	### Two kinds of failure
41	
42	A condition we can name in advance, and that the person can act on, is an expected error. It is designed for when the feature is built, like any other part of the feature, once we have verified how it shows up: from the other side's documentation or a real answer, not from memory.
43	
44	Everything else is a surprise, an unexpected error. No handling is written for it, it stops the work, and it is reported with everything known. The reporting must be complete, because a surprise that is not reported is lost. A failure that ends in a log line alone, a default value, or a sentence for "anything else" is a hole. Reading the code can check this: from each place work starts, follow a failure up to the handler that reports it.
45	
46	Reports then show which surprises to fix, and which are really conditions that need a design.
47	
48	Every failure is written to the log, expected or unexpected. The log is kept as well as the report, never in its place.
49	
50	### Expected errors
51	
52	- Each has an entry in the expected-errors table: the cause, what the person sees, and what they can do next. A new entry needs Kenneth's yes; quote his words in the commit message.
53	- The test is what the person can do next. If the answer is "nothing" or only "try again later", the error is unexpected. An AI provider or our own server being slow, overloaded, down or limiting us is unexpected: the person can do nothing about any of them.
54	- Two causes that leave the person doing the same thing do not get separate sentences, codes or branches.
55	- A cause is "out of credits" or "no network". A status code, an exception type, or "the request was not valid" is not a cause.
56	- Each entry has a test, and each occurrence is counted.
57	- Handle them with normal control flow, not exceptions.
58	
59	### Unexpected errors
60	
61	- Write no code for them. Do not catch one, give it a default value, retry it, or give it a sentence of its own. Each of those is a guess about a failure nobody understands. It hides the failure and loses where it came from.
62	- Let the failure stop the work and travel up unchanged.
63	- A failure that arrives as a value, such as a status code, stops nothing by itself. Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop. Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it.
64	- One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure through the one reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side", with nothing more specific. No other code reports.
65	- A tool call that fails is shown as failed in the turn's activity line, its error goes to the AI model, and the turn goes on; no dialog opens. When the failure is the app's own and not the model's mistake, it is also reported, and only if the person has turned automatic reports on.
66	- When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected.
67	- The report carries as much as is known: the other side's status, request id and error text, and the request's own facts, such as the user, the chat, the turn and the model. The person is told none of it.
68	- Never record a failure as a success.
69	- A log line is not a report: it reaches nobody.
70	
71	### Catching
72	
73	- Catch an error only when it is an expected one and the code can recover from it, or at a boundary to translate it or add context, and then rethrow.
74	- Keep lower-level operations strict; the caller that owns the workflow enforces their preconditions.
75	- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering.
76	
77	### Checks
78	
79	- An agent reads the changed code against these rules and asks one question wherever the code decides what happened: can the person do something about it, and did Kenneth decide what they are told?
80	- Do not sort unexpected failures into kinds for the person, and do not bring Kenneth a question about the wording of a failure the person can do nothing about. On 2026-11-16 the code that kept five "try again" sentences apart was deleted for this reason.
81	- To audit a commit range, use the `error-handling` skill (`.claude/skills/error-handling/`). To check production for a period, use the `jusprin-production-check` skill in the tsd-enterprise repository.
82	
83	## Build Commands
84	
85	Build the Release configuration unless asked otherwise.
86	
87	```bash
88	# macOS
89	cmake --build build/arm64 --config Release --target all --
90	
91	# Linux
92	cmake --build build --config Release --target all --
93	
94	# Windows
95	cmake --build . --config Release --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
96	```
97	
98	Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.
99	
100	### Building on a shared machine
101	
102	Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.
103	
104	- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
105	- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
106	- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
107	- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
108	- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
109	- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
110	- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.
111	- Before building against a dependency folder built earlier, such as the main checkout's `deps/build/arm64`, run `scripts/deps_current.sh <folder>`. It rebuilds the libraries whose `deps/` recipe changed since that folder was built.
112	
113	## Testing
114	
115	Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/`; see [tests/AGENTS.md](tests/AGENTS.md) for where a new test belongs and the conventions to follow.
116	
117	```bash
118	cd build && ctest -C Release --output-on-failure    # all tests
119	ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r -C Release       # individual suite
120	ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print -C Release
121	```
122	
123	Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake); Moonraker and OctoPrint: `tests/printer_hosts/README.md` (Docker). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.
124	
125	## Documentation
126	
127	- Docs live in `docs/`; the high-level design of a subsystem goes in `docs/HLSD/<subsystem>.md`.
128	- Describe the design as it stands — what the subsystem does, why it exists, and the constraints that shape it. Not the route that got there: no phases, task lists, status markers, or "before/after this PR" framing.
129	- Planning and investigation output (brainstorms, superpowers design and plan docs) stays in `docs/superpowers/`, which is gitignored. Never commit it.
130	- Write a doc only when the design is not evident from the code, and when a change invalidates an existing one, update it in the same PR.
131	
132	## Code Style
133	
134	- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
135	- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
136	- Include what you use: include the header for every symbol a file uses, and keep headers compilable on their own. Never rely on the precompiled header or a transitive include. The `clang-tidy` CI job enforces this on changed lines; run the same check locally with `scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh` (`scripts\run_clang_tidy.ps1` on Windows), which sets up everything it needs
137	- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
138	- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.
139	- Wording the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca or OrcaSlicer: the model speaks as the app, and a second name reads as a second program. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards this too. Log lines may name Orca. A throw may only if it never reaches the model: tool results forward save and open errors as they are, and the guard does not see those strings.
140	- Always use `SetSizerAndFit(sizer)` instead of `SetSizer(sizer)` on top level window. Unless `SetSizer` must be called before the full layout is built, call `sizer->SetSizeHints(window)` afterwards in this case.
141	
142	## Key Entry Points
143	
144	- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
145	- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
146	- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
147	- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
148	- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
149	- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`
150	
151	## JusPrin Production UI
152	
153	- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
154	- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
155	- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
156	- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
157	- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
158	- Before designing a screen or writing any on-screen text, follow `agent-docs/jusprin/design-guidelines.md`: whole-screen boards with real strings, the wording rule, and a cold-reader check on screenshots before and after building.
159	- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.
160	
161	## Critical Constraints
162	
163	- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
164	- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
165	- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
166	- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app
167	
168	## Pull requests
169	
170	Before opening a pull request or posting on GitHub, read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), including its "If you are an AI agent" section.
171	
172	## Code review focus areas
173	
174	- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
175	- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
176	- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
177	- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
178	- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
179	- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
180	- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
181	- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.
182	- For profile changes (`resources/profiles/<Vendor>/**`), check that `version` in the sibling `resources/profiles/<Vendor>.json` was bumped.
183	- For new or changed UI strings, check they follow [Writing translatable strings in the source](#writing-translatable-strings-in-the-source): no concatenated fragments, plural forms for counts, contexts for ambiguous words.
184	- For translation changes (`localization/i18n/**/*.po`), check that recurring terms match the [Localization glossary](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_glossary.md) for that language.
185	
186	## Localization & translations
187	
188	Catalogs live in `localization/i18n/<lang>/OrcaSlicer_<lang>.po`; the template is `OrcaSlicer.pot`.
189	See the [Localization guide](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_guide.md) for the human-facing version of these principles.
190	
191	### Writing translatable strings in the source
192	
193	Translators see one msgid at a time and cannot change the code around it, so each message must be complete in a single msgid. Use the wrapper that fits instead of assembling text from pieces:
194	
195	- **One msgid per sentence, with placeholders.** Never build a message by concatenating translated fragments (`_L("A") + name + _L(" is B")`) or by splicing a translated word such as `_L("left")` into another sentence: the translator can't reorder or inflect the parts. Write `format(_L("%1% is too close to others"), name)`.
196	- **A count needs a plural form.** Don't write `file(s)` or leave a verb unchanged after a number. Use `_L_PLURAL("%1% object", "%1% objects", n)`. libslic3r has no plural lookup, so word the message so it doesn't depend on a count, or build it in the GUI.
197	- **An ambiguous word needs a context.** When a short string means different things in different places (verb or noun, a mode name, a CAD term), give each sense its own context with `_L_CONTEXT`/`_u8L_CONTEXT`/`L_CONTEXT`. Keep the most common sense without a context so its existing translations stay valid.
198	- **Mark every user-visible string** (`_L`/`_u8L`, or `L` where it is translated later) and list new source files in `localization/i18n/list.txt`: files that aren't listed are never extracted.
199	- Add a `// TRN` comment above a new string whose meaning or placeholders aren't obvious.
200	- Never choose behavior by comparing translated text; compare ids or flags.
201	
202	See `.claude/skills/orca-translations/references/source-audit.md` for the full checklist.
203	
204	### Terminology
205	
206	- Use the [Localization glossary](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_glossary.md) as the source of truth for recurring terms, so the same English term is always rendered the same way within a language, and terms that must stay in English (brand/product names, acronyms, materials, file formats, G-code tokens, macros/variables/identifiers) are not translated.
207	- If a term's established translation changes, update both the affected `.po` files and the glossary (`developer_reference/glossary/<lang>.tsv` in the wiki, then regenerate) so they stay in sync.
208	- Translate the *meaning*, not the words. Check what the string actually controls before translating it — English reuses one word for different things. `Flow ratio` (multiplier), `Flow Rate` (throughput) and `Flow Dynamics` (pressure compensation) are three different terms; `extruder` may mean the toolhead, the feeder motor, or the nozzle depending on the string.
209	- Reuse one template per recurring message shape (`Failed to connect to …`, `Are you sure you want to …?`), even where the English wording varies.
210	
211	### Editing rules
212	
213	- Only edit `msgstr` — **never** change `msgid`, and never "fix" wrong English in the translation alone. Report the source string instead.
214	- Preserve exactly: placeholders (`%s`, `%d`, `%1%`, `%zu`, `%%`), every `\n` (count *and* position, including leading/trailing), leading/trailing spaces, HTML tags, `℃`, and the file's encoding and line endings.
215	- **Never reorder positional arguments** in a `c-format` string. If the msgid is `%d` then `%s`, that order must hold — swapping them breaks at runtime.
216	- `msgctxt` separates homonyms — always read it. `Back`/`Camera View` is the rear view of the 3D navigator, while `Back`/`Navigation` is the go-back button; `Top` exists in the *Alignment*, *Layers* and *Camera View* senses.
217	- When a string needs disambiguating, add context in the source (`_L_CONTEXT`/`_u8L_CONTEXT`), don't work around it in the translation.
218	- A literal `%` inside a string xgettext flagged `possible-c-format` will fail `msgfmt`. Fix it with a `// xgettext:no-c-format, no-boost-format` comment above the string in the source — do not mangle the translation or use `%%` in text that is never passed through printf.
219	- Plural entries: read `nplurals` from the catalog's `Plural-Forms` header (it is **not** always 2 — ja/ko/zh/th/vi use 1, ru/cs/pl/lt use 3, uk uses 4). Each form must be genuinely inflected for its quantity; repeating one sentence across all forms is a bug in Slavic/Baltic languages, though it is correct for Turkish and Hungarian.
220	- An entry whose `msgstr` equals its `msgid` is untranslated even though it is not empty; a plural entry with any empty form is likewise incomplete.
221	- Mark machine-produced translations with an `# AI Translated` translator comment. Don't add it to a human translation you didn't actually rewrite.
222	- When you can't be sure of a machine translation's meaning or UI wording, also add `# Needs human review: <what to check>`. Never use `fuzzy` for this — fuzzy entries are hidden from users.
223	- Don't reflow or re-wrap unrelated entries — keep the diff limited to the strings you changed.
224	
225	### Verifying
226	
227	- `scripts/run_gettext.bat --full` (Windows) regenerates the template, merges every catalog and compiles the `.mo` files. It must exit 0.
228	- Or check a single catalog with `msgfmt --check-format --check-header -o <out>.mo localization/i18n/<lang>/OrcaSlicer_<lang>.po`. Without `--check-header`, msgfmt skips the placeholder check in plural forms.
229	- Fuzzy entries are not shown to users. If you correct one, clear its `fuzzy` flag, otherwise the fix never ships.

# Test suite rules

Rules for writing tests under `tests/`. [CATCH2.md](CATCH2.md) is the Catch2 reference. Building and running the suites is covered on the wiki, at <https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_test.html>.

## The suites

- `libslic3r`: the core library. Geometry, meshes, file formats, config and presets, Clipper, algorithms, data structures.
- `fff_print`: the FFF slicing pipeline, from a `Model` plus config through `Print` and `PrintObject` to emitted G-code.
- `sla_print`: SLA support-tree and pad geometry, support-point generation, raycast.
- `libnest2d`: 2D nesting and packing.
- `slic3rutils`: the Python plugin system and its slicing-pipeline bindings.
- `filament_group`: filament-to-extruder grouping, checked against golden files.
- `cli`: end-to-end runs of the built `orca-slicer` binary, Linux only. These tests carry the `RequiresApp` label, which the CI unit-test job excludes because it receives only `build/tests`; run them with `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release -L RequiresApp`.

## Building and running

Tests are off by default, so the build has to be told to include them.

- Windows: `build_win.bat -ds --run-tests`, which builds the dependencies and the tests and runs them (`-l -x` for the clang-cl and Ninja build CI uses)
- macOS: `./build_release_macos.sh -s -a arm64 -T`, which builds and runs them
- Linux: `./build_linux.sh -t`, then `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release`

Rebuild a single suite with `cmake --build build --config Release --target <suite>_tests`. Visual Studio, Xcode and the Ninja Multi-Config generator that `build_linux.sh` uses are all multi-configuration, so `ctest` needs `-C` on every platform; without it, tests registered with plain `add_test()` lose their labels and report "Not Run".

## Where a test goes

- Pick the suite by the production code the test exercises, not by how the test is written.
- A property of a class that holds with no `Print` involved belongs in `libslic3r`. Behavior that depends on print settings, or produces or consumes G-code or slicing state, belongs in `fff_print`.
- One file per subsystem, named `test_<subsystem>.cpp`. It owns every test for that subsystem, whether the test reads in-memory state or generated output.
- When you add a file, list it in that suite's `CMakeLists.txt` in the same change.

## Use the existing helpers

Check these before writing your own setup or output-parsing code.

- `tests/test_utils.hpp` is shared by every suite. `load_model()` loads a mesh from `tests/data/`, and `ScopedTemporaryFile` gives a temp path that removes itself.
- `fff_print/test_helpers.hpp` builds and slices a `Print` and parses the emitted G-code. Read it before writing an fff_print test rather than assembling a `Print` by hand.
- The other suites have their own: `sla_print/sla_test_utils.hpp`, `libnest2d/libnest2d_test_utils.hpp`, `slic3rutils/plugin_test_utils.hpp`, `filament_group/fg_test_utils.hpp`. `libslic3r` has none and uses the shared header.
- Test data lives in `tests/data/` and is reached through the `TEST_DATA_DIR` define. Wrap it in `std::string(...)` before joining a path onto it.

"""Stand-in Sentry server: saves every POST body it gets, one file each."""
import gzip
import http.server
import os
import sys
import time
import zlib

OUT = sys.argv[1]
PORT = int(sys.argv[2])
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)


class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get('Content-Length') or 0)
        body = self.rfile.read(length)
        encoding = self.headers.get('Content-Encoding', '')
        try:
            if encoding == 'gzip':
                body = gzip.decompress(body)
            elif encoding == 'deflate':
                body = zlib.decompress(body)
        except Exception:
            pass
        name = '%d-%s.bin' % (time.time_ns(), self.path.strip('/').replace('/', '_').split('?')[0])
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, name), 'wb') as f:
            f.write(self.path.encode() + b'\n' + str(self.headers).encode() + b'\n' + body)
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b'{"id":"00000000000000000000000000000000"}')

    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):
        sys.stderr.write('%s %s\n' % (self.command, self.path))


http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', PORT), Handler).serve_forever()

The inbox is clear of Sentry emails. Two alert emails were still there for issues handled in this session, and I moved both to the trash rather than deleting them for good:

- **MOONRAKER-OBICO-VP**, the ffmpeg exit with code 0.
- **OBICO-SERVER-B2N**, the stuck chat.

The alert emails for the file-drop crash (JUSPRIN-APP-7) and the "cannot write" error (JUSPRIN-APP-8) were already in the trash. I logged both moves in the triage skill's email log.

**Naming users in JusPrin crash reports, using the account number only:**

- **Signed in:** every report and crash would name the person by their account number on the server. The app saves the number when someone signs in, and also when it re-checks an old sign-in at startup, so people who signed in before this change get it too. Signing out removes the number from reports.
- **Signed out:** reports keep the Sentry library's own random id for that installation.
- **Every report:** it also carries that installation id as a tag named `installation_id`, so one person's reports from before and after signing in can be matched.

The work is in a separate worktree at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/sentry-user-id`, on the branch `claude/sentry-user-id`, made from the development branch. Nothing is committed.

**Tested so far:** all 63 sign-in test cases pass. Those include one new test: a sign-in check that comes back without an account number stops the sign-in and saves nothing. The server has returned that number since July 2025, so this shouldn't affect anyone.

**Not tested yet:** whether a real report from the running app carries the right ids. The full app is still building, slowly, because the machine is busy. When it's done I'll:

1. Run it against the local dev server, with reports going to a stand-in for Sentry on this Mac, so no test issues land on sentry.obico.io.
2. Check a crash report while signed out: it should carry only the installation id.
3. Sign in with a throwaway local test account (number 77) and check a second crash report: it should carry the number 77 and the same installation id tag.

content.text:
JusPrin crash reports now say who the person is. If they're signed in, the report carries their account number. If not, it carries the install id the app already kept, `jusprin_install_id`, which the server also records each time the app starts. I used that id because you asked to reuse an existing one before making a new one. Every report also carries the install id as a tag named `install_id`, so one person's reports from before and after signing in can be matched. Nothing else about the account is sent.

**What I tested.** I built the app and ran it on a throwaway data folder against the local dev server. Its reports went to a stand-in for Sentry on this Mac, so nothing reached sentry.obico.io. Then I crashed it on purpose:

- **Signed out:** the crash report's person was the app's install id, and the `install_id` tag matched it.
- **Signed in** as local test account 77: the person was `77`, and the tag still had the same install id.
- **Sign-in tests:** all 63 test cases pass. Two of them check that the account number is saved after a sign-in. One new test checks that a sign-in check answered without the number stops the sign-in and saves nothing.

**Not tested:**

- Signing in and out by hand in the app. For the signed-in crash I wrote the account number into the settings myself. The code that saves it after a real sign-in is covered by the unit tests.
- An ordinary error report, as opposed to a crash. Both read the same person and tag from the Sentry library, so I'd expect the same result.
- The project's lint check, because it needs a newer clang-tidy than this Mac has. GitHub's checks will run it on the pull request.

I deleted the test token and deactivated the local test account.

**Where it is.** The code is in the worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/sentry-user-id`, on the branch `claude/sentry-user-id`, made from the development branch. It touches 8 files and nothing is committed.

**Decision needed: how should people who are already signed in when they update get their account number?** The app only re-checks a saved sign-in when someone opens Preferences or signs in again, so until then their reports carry only the install id. This is your call because one option changes the server.

- **The server adds the number:** the server adds the account number to the account details the Home page already loads on every start, and the app reads it from there. That's about one line on the server plus a little app code. It needs a server release, and it fixes everyone on their first start after updating.
- **The app asks at startup:** the app makes one extra call to the server when it has a saved sign-in but no number. It's app only, but it adds a call to startup and needs a rule for when that call fails, for example offline.

My pick is the server option, because it reuses a call that already happens. Should I add the number to the server's account details?
the simplest way possible. Our goal here is not to get 100% accurate. Our goal is to use a simple solution that works. Moving forward, if it can work retrospectively, great. Otherwise, don't bother.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Pull requests

Before opening a pull request or posting on GitHub, read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), including its "If you are an AI agent" section.

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.
- For profile changes (`resources/profiles/<Vendor>/**`), check that `version` in the sibling `resources/profiles/<Vendor>.json` was bumped.
- For new or changed UI strings, check they follow [Writing translatable strings in the source](#writing-translatable-strings-in-the-source): no concatenated fragments, plural forms for counts, contexts for ambiguous words.
- For translation changes (`localization/i18n/**/*.po`), check that recurring terms match the [Localization glossary](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_glossary.md) for that language.

## Localization & translations

Catalogs live in `localization/i18n/<lang>/OrcaSlicer_<lang>.po`; the template is `OrcaSlicer.pot`.
See the [Localization guide](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_guide.md) for the human-facing version of these principles.

### Writing translatable strings in the source

Translators see one msgid at a time and cannot change the code around it, so each message must be complete in a single msgid. Use the wrapper that fits instead of assembling text from pieces:

- **One msgid per sentence, with placeholders.** Never build a message by concatenating translated fragments (`_L("A") + name + _L(" is B")`) or by splicing a translated word such as `_L("left")` into another sentence: the translator can't reorder or inflect the parts. Write `format(_L("%1% is too close to others"), name)`.
- **A count needs a plural form.** Don't write `file(s)` or leave a verb unchanged after a number. Use `_L_PLURAL("%1% object", "%1% objects", n)`. libslic3r has no plural lookup, so word the message so it doesn't depend on a count, or build it in the GUI.
- **An ambiguous word needs a context.** When a short string means different things in different places (verb or noun, a mode name, a CAD term), give each sense its own context with `_L_CONTEXT`/`_u8L_CONTEXT`/`L_CONTEXT`. Keep the most common sense without a context so its existing translations stay valid.
- **Mark every user-visible string** (`_L`/`_u8L`, or `L` where it is translated later) and list new source files in `localization/i18n/list.txt`: files that aren't listed are never extracted.
- Add a `// TRN` comment above a new string whose meaning or placeholders aren't obvious.
- Never choose behavior by comparing translated text; compare ids or flags.

Crash and error reports name the person: the account number, or else the install
Sentry showed how many reports an issue had but not how many people it hit,
because the app named nobody. Kenneth asked for the signed-in account where
there is one and an id of the install where there is none, and chose to send
the account number only, not the email.

Every report and crash now carries a Sentry user id: the account number when a
JusPrin account is signed in, otherwise the app's own install id
(jusprin_install_id, from Updates::install_id), which the server already
records on every launch. The install id is also a tag, install_id, so one
person's reports from before and after signing in can be matched.

The account number comes from the sign-in check (/jusprin/api/me/, user.id)
and is stored beside the account's email as jusprin_account_id. An answer
without it is unexpected and stores nothing. Signing out erases it and the
reports go back to the install id. At startup the reports name the account
stored when the app last closed.

Someone already signed in before this update is named by account number only
after signing in again or opening Preferences, which re-checks the sign-in.
Kenneth chose not to add anything for that.

Tested:
- The agent account tests pass (63 cases, 850 assertions), including the
  stored number after a browser sign-in and after a stored sign-in is
  re-checked, and a new case where the check answers without a number.
- In the built app against a local server, crashes sent to a stand-in Sentry
  receiver: signed out, user.id was the install id; with account 77 stored,
  user.id was 77. The install_id tag was the install id both times.
- Not tested: signing in and out by hand in the running app, an ordinary
  error report (it reads the same user and tag as a crash), and
  scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh (this machine has clang-tidy 20.1.5, not 22.1.8).
EOF
